name: Tetrapeptide-5
lead: Tetrapeptide-5, usually listed on labels as acetyl tetrapeptide-5, is a short four-amino-acid peptide used in eye creams and gels aimed at puffy eyelids and under-eye bags. People use it to make the eye area look smoother and less swollen.

It is a cosmetic ingredient rather than a drug. In a 2021 laboratory study of five cosmetic peptides on skin cells, acetyl tetrapeptide-5 at 100 micrograms per milliliter showed activity on angiotensin-converting enzyme 1, one of the measures the researchers used to assess anti-aging and protective formulas [1]. Published human trials specific to the peptide are limited.

chain: Applied to the eyelid and under-eye skin in a cream or gel
Peptide acts on fluid and glycation-related pathways in skin
Eye area looks less puffy and smoother
angle.text: Tetrapeptide-5 is applied in eye products to reduce the look of morning puffiness and bags. Users apply it as part of an eye-care routine alongside other ingredients such as caffeine.

paras: Acetyl tetrapeptide-5 appears in eye gels and creams marketed for puffiness and dark under-eye appearance. It is often paired with other eye-area actives in the same formula.

Ingredient suppliers describe the peptide as acting on swelling-related pathways in the skin around the eye, including angiotensin-converting enzyme activity and glycation. The 2021 cell study cited above measured activity on angiotensin-converting enzyme 1 for this peptide [1].
No studies found. Laboratory work on skin cells has tested the peptide alone and in cosmetic peptide mixtures [1].

As a topical cosmetic ingredient it is generally used in leave-on eye products at low concentrations; product labels advise avoiding contact with the eyes' interior and stopping use if irritation occurs.

refs.title: Protective and Anti-Aging Effects of 5 Cosmeceutical Peptide Mixtures on Hydrogen Peroxide-Induced Premature Senescence in Human Skin Fibroblasts

card.summary: A short cosmetic peptide in eye creams that people use to make puffy under-eyes look smoother and less swollen.

quick.overview:
Tetrapeptide-5 is a four-amino-acid peptide added to eye creams and gels. People use it to reduce the look of puffy eyelids and under-eye bags.

It is found in over-the-counter products and is often combined with other eye-area ingredients.
quick.mechanism: Ingredient makers describe it as acting on swelling-related pathways and glycation in the thin skin around the eyes. A 2021 cell study measured its activity on angiotensin-converting enzyme 1 [1].
quick.risks: It is a topical cosmetic ingredient with a low reported irritation profile in leave-on eye products. Labels advise stopping use if irritation develops.
